extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and practitioners (attorneys/agents) and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on preparing, correcting, and submitting an Application Data Sheet (ADS) for U.S. patent applications, including required sections, bibliographic content, signing, correction procedures, and how ADS interacts with other forms and documents (e.g., oath/declaration, PCT/PLT forms).

rubrics_metrics.name: ADS must be titled and contain required section headings
rubrics_metrics.description: An application data sheet must be titled "Application Data Sheet" and must contain all of the section headings listed in paragraph (b) of this section, with any appropriate data for each section heading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an application data sheet is provided, the application data sheet is part of the provisional or nonprovisional application for which it has been submitted. Supplemental ADS must be titled "Supplemental Application Data Sheet," include all section headings listed in paragraph (b), include all appropriate data for each heading, and identify the information being changed (preferably with underlining for insertions and strike-through or brackets for text removed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant information content
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant information includes the name (either natural person or juristic entity), residence, mailing address, and citizenship of each applicant; the name must include the family name and at least one given name without abbreviation together with any other given name or initial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant is not an inventor, applicant information must also include the applicant's authority to apply on behalf of the inventor (see §§ 1.42, 1.43, and 1.47). The heading should be left blank if the applicant is the inventor or remaining joint inventor(s). Changes to applicant name or identity must comply with 37 CFR 1.46(c) and may require submission of an ADS showing the corrected/updated name in the applicant information section in accordance with 37 CFR 1.76(c)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee information content and legal effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignee information includes the name (either person or juristic entity) and address of the assignee of the entire right, title, and interest in an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing assignee information in the ADS does not substitute for compliance with any requirement of 37 CFR part 3 to have an assignment recorded by the Office; assignment information must be recorded to have legal effect. Inclusion of assignee information is considered a request to include such information on the patent application publication. Assignees who are the applicant will appear on the publication as the applicant and only need to separately provide assignee information in the assignee section if identification as an assignee is also desired on the publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence information requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence information includes the correspondence address, which may be indicated by reference to a customer number, to which correspondence is to be directed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correspondence address entries should follow § 1.33(a) format; changes to correspondence address are governed by § 1.33(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application information required in ADS
rubrics_metrics.description: Application information includes the title of the invention, a suggested classification by class and subclass, the Technology Center to which the subject matter is assigned, the total number of drawing sheets, a suggested drawing figure for publication (in a nonprovisional application), any docket number assigned to the application, and the type of application (e.g., utility, plant, design, reissue, provisional).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested classification and Technology Center information should be supplied for provisional applications whether or not claims are present, and should be based upon the disclosure if claims are absent. The Office may not use suggested classification/figure for publication but may use the ADS-provided data for front page continuity data when not present in the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative information content and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Representative information includes the registration number of each practitioner having a power of attorney in the application (preferably by reference to a customer number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing representative information in the ADS does not constitute a power of attorney in the application (see § 1.32), because the Office does not expect the ADS to be executed by the party who may appoint a power of attorney.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic priority (benefit) information content
rubrics_metrics.description: Domestic priority information includes the application number, the filing date, the status (including patent number if available), and relationship of each application for which a benefit is claimed under 35 U.S.C. 119(e), 120, 121, or 365(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing this information in the ADS constitutes the specific reference required by 35 U.S.C. 119(e) or 120 and need not otherwise be made part of the specification. No continuity data will be included in the first sentence(s) of the specification if applicant does not provide it there. Pre-AIA, this does not apply to provisional applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign priority information content
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign priority information includes the application number, country, and filing date of each foreign application for which priority is claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing this information in the ADS constitutes the claim for priority as required by 35 U.S.C. 119(b) and § 1.55(a). Pre-AIA this does not apply to provisional applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrected and supplemental ADS formatting for edits
rubrics_metrics.description: Any corrected ADS must identify the information that is being changed with underlining for insertions and strike-through or brackets for text removed (except that identification is not required for an ADS included with an initial submission under 35 U.S.C. 371).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In general, identification of the information being changed should be made relative to the most recent filing receipt. A corrected ADS may include all section headings or only those sections (including headings) containing changed or updated information. Examples: to correct an inventor's residence, show the incorrect info with strike-through and the corrected residence with underlining.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and effect of submitting corrected ADS
rubrics_metrics.description: A corrected ADS may be submitted until payment of the issue fee to either correct or update information in a previously submitted ADS, or in an inventor’s oath or declaration, or otherwise of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A corrected ADS filed after final rejection or allowance is not entered as a matter of right; such amendments must comply with 37 CFR 1.116 (after final) or 1.312 (after allowance). Corrected ADS should be filed with a request for a corrected filing receipt unless accompanied by some other request (e.g., 1.48, 1.46(c), or submission of a power of attorney).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on Web-based corrected ADS use
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of the corrected Web-based ADS is recommended because it will pre-populate and create a PDF with appropriate strike-through and underlining.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A corrected Web-based ADS, however, is not permitted in national stage applications under 35 U.S.C. 371, provisional applications, plant applications, reexamination proceedings, and supplemental examinations under 35 U.S.C. 257. Quick Start Guide references are provided for corrected Web-based ADS guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to add a benefit or priority claim in a corrected ADS
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the most recent filing receipt does not include a benefit claim or priority claim, a corrected ADS submitted to add the benefit or priority claim must identify the addition of the benefit claim or priority claim with underlining relative to the most recent filing receipt (i.e., the entire benefit or priority claim must be underlined).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the ADS previously identified an incorrect benefit claim and the most recent filing receipt included the incorrect claim, the corrected ADS should identify deletions with strike-through or brackets and additions with underlining. If deleting a claim, the corrected ADS must identify the deletion with strike-through or brackets and applicants should consider potential consequences (e.g., exposure to new prior art or being viewed as intentionally waiving the claim). A petition for unintentionally delayed claim under 37 CFR 1.78(c)/(e) or 1.55(e) may be required if submitted outside the statutory time periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolution of inconsistent information — general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: For inconsistencies between information supplied by an ADS and other documents, the most recent submitted information will govern (control), except as otherwise provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes inconsistencies between an ADS, an amendment to the specification, a designation of correspondence address, or an oath/declaration. The ADS is intended to be the means by which applicant provides complete bibliographic information; when another document submitted concurrently contains more accurate information, submit a corrected ADS to conform the ADS to the correct information.

rubrics_metrics.name: ADS governs when provided concurrently or inconsistent with certain international/PLT/PCT forms
rubrics_metrics.description: The information in the ADS will govern when the inconsistent information is supplied at the same time by a designation of correspondence address or the inventor’s oath/declaration. The ADS will also govern when inconsistent with the information supplied at any time in a PCT Request Form, PLT Model International Request Form, or related PLT model recordation forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.76(d)(2) makes ADS the controlling source for many bibliographic inconsistencies; however, special exceptions exist (e.g., inventorship/citizenship).

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath/declaration controls inventorship and citizenship
rubrics_metrics.description: The oath or declaration under § 1.63 (or pre-AIA § 1.63/1.67) governs inconsistencies with the ADS in the naming of inventors (§ 1.41(a)(1)) and setting forth their citizenship (35 U.S.C. 115).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even though the Office captures bibliographic information from the ADS, the oath/declaration still governs inventorship and citizenship; changes to inventorship must be done by request under § 1.48.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office will capture bibliographic information from ADS and not generally review oath for consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will capture bibliographic information from the application data sheet; it will generally not review the inventor’s oath or declaration to determine if the bibliographic information contained therein is consistent with information provided in an ADS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captured bibliographic information derived from an ADS containing errors may be corrected if applicant submits a request therefor and a supplemental ADS. Examples: if ADS lists inventors A,B,C but an oath correctly identifies A,B, the Office will capture A,B,C from the ADS and include that on the filing receipt; to correct inventorship, applicant must file under § 1.48.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirement for ADS and effects of unsigned ADS
rubrics_metrics.description: An application data sheet must be signed in compliance with 37 CFR 1.33(b). An unsigned ADS will be treated only as a transmittal letter and will not be effective to provide the name of the inventor for any invention claimed in the application, name as the applicant an assignee/obligated assignee/person with proprietary interest, make a claim to foreign priority (37 CFR 1.55), or make a claim to domestic benefit (37 CFR 1.78).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-AIA 37 CFR 1.76(e) makes signing essential to effectuate the substantive bibliographic entries in the ADS. (Pre-AIA, 1.76(e) was not applicable to applications filed before Sept 16, 2012.)

rubrics_metrics.name: PLT/PCT forms can substitute for ADS for certain items
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.76(f) and (g) provide that requirements for presentation of priority/benefit claims, references to previously filed applications, and the name of the applicant in an ADS will be satisfied by presentation of such information in Patent Law Treaty Model International Request Forms or the PCT Request Form in certain contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: (1) presentation of priority/benefit claim in PLT Model International Request Form satisfies § 1.55/1.78; (2) reference to previously filed application in PLT form satisfies § 1.57(a); (3) name of applicant in PLT/PCT forms satisfies § 1.46. For national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371, the PCT Request Form contained in the international application or presence of the claim on the front page of publication may satisfy ADS requirements, but submissions during the national stage may require an ADS to add/correct information. If a PCT Request Form is submitted in an application under 35 U.S.C. 111, it must be accompanied by a clear indication that treatment as a §111 application is desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: ADS inclusion constitutes part of application and influences front-page data
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application data sheet is provided, the application data sheet is part of the provisional or nonprovisional application and continuity/front-page data may be taken from the ADS (rather than the specification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If continuity data is included in an ADS but not in the specification, the patent front page continuity data will be taken from the ADS. No continuity data will be placed in the first sentence(s) of the specification if applicant does not provide it there.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes to applicant identity require compliance with multiple rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If submitted during the national stage or otherwise, any request to change the applicant must include an ADS specifying the applicant in the applicant information section and comply with 37 CFR 3.71 and 3.73; the application data sheet must comply with the provisions for correcting and updating an ADS set forth in 37 CFR 1.76(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests to correct or update the name of the applicant must include an ADS under 1.76 specifying the corrected or updated name in accordance with 1.76(c)(2). A change in applicant recorded pursuant to Hague Agreement Article 16(1)(ii) will change applicant name in a nonprovisional international design application.
